To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the top partner is constrained at the 2σ level by the global fit and that TLEP can probe the top partner in multi-TeV mass region.

the minimal fermionic model of the top partners can accommodate the current Higgs data and electroweak constraints, while at the same time the mass of the top partners is bounded from below by the indirect constraints.

1) the top partner is excluded up to 830~GeV by the global fit of the Higgs data, the B s → μ+μ− measurements and the electowek precision observables; 2) under the current constraints, the fine tuning measure is less than ~9%; and 3) the branching ratio of the T → t Z decay is bounded between 0.14 and 0.25.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of top quark and its partner in the context of a supersymmetric model with an extended gauge sector, which is motivated by a possible solution to the hierarchy problem.
the indirect constraints on top partner within the fermionic top partner models and the fine-tuning problem.
the indirect constraints on the minimal fermionic extension of the SM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the top partner mass up to 1.5 TeV can be excluded by the future measurements at the LHC or TLEP.
the current Higgs and electroweak measurements at the LHC are not sufficient to probe the top partner mass up to the multi-TeV region.
a top partner with the current mass bound from direct search is not natural.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the top partner mass up to 1.2 TeV is excluded at the LHC, while the top partner mass below 2.5 TeV is excluded by the Higgs data at the TLEP.
the current Higgs data, electroweak data and the B s → μ+μ- data provide the strongest indirect constraint on the top partners.
the top partner can be found at the 240 GeV ILC and 100 TeV FCC, and the top partner mass can be constrained at the 14 TeV LHC and 240 GeV FCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current Higgs data and the electrowek precision observables already provide strong indirect constraints on the minimal fermionic extension of the Standard Model, which is complementary to the LHC direct search.

indirect constraints on the fermionic top partner are much stronger than the direct ones at the LHC, and the future precision measurements of Higgs properties at TLEP will provide an important complementary probe of the fermionic top partners.
